title: I was explaining Fonder backwards
body: The first homepage mostly explained what Fonder could do: films, recipes, developing, controls. All true, and all beside the point.

I'm not building Fonder because iPhones need more filters. I'm building it because phone cameras became incredibly good while taking photos somehow became less fun. Somewhere in writing marketing notes this week, that stopped being a feeling and became the actual brief: the feeling of film, not just the look.

So the site changed too. The homepage now starts with what Fonder tries to bring back — limitation, anticipation, imperfection, and seeing a whole roll at once — and the features moved down a level, where they belong: as proof, not as the pitch. The recipes page learned to talk about moments before colour science, every film got a line about when you'd load it, and the whole site now reads in Vietnamese as well, my own translation.
